what_happened: In job zyqr, the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The last attempt of this job family was refused at admission. crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs gained text that looks like an email address outside the personal-data allow-list. It was almost certainly an SSH-style remote such as [email]:owner/repo in a test. The user told the reading to use https://github.com/owner/repo URLs in tests and docs, or an allowed address such as noreply@example.com, and not to add a new address. The earlier decisions stand: open or update the job's pull request at verification start, and skip silently when there is no GitHub origin.
cause: The email rule lives in admission's allow-list and nowhere the reading or the producer can see. SSH remote strings such as git@host:owner/repo are natural test fixtures for code that parses GitHub origins, and they match the email pattern. Nothing scans the diff for the pattern before admission, and the reading does not list fixture forms to avoid. Admission is the first place the rule is applied, so the refusal came only after the work was done, and a user correction was needed to carry the rule into the next reading.
prevention: Run the admission email-literal scan as a pre-commit check inside the producer's own loop, over the diff or the working tree. A hit should fail fast with the offending file and line and tell the writer to use https URLs or an allowed address. Show the producer the same allow-list and the rule in its prompt, with a note that SSH remote strings count as emails. That catches the whole class, whether the literal is a git author, a bot identity or an SSH fixture, before admission refuses the job.
proposed_request: Implement: at verification start, open or update the job's pull request, with the candidate as head, through the same host seam `athena land` uses. Opening it must not merge anything. If origin is missing or is not a GitHub remote, skip silently with no warning line. A real host error on a GitHub remote prints a warning and is non-fatal. Constraints: in all code, tests and docs, do not write any email-like string, including SSH remotes such as [email]:owner/repo. Use https://github.com/owner/repo URLs for GitHub remotes in fixtures. If an address is truly needed, use only noreply@example.com, and add no new address. Before finishing, scan your diff for any string matching an email pattern and remove it. Acceptance: tests cover a GitHub https origin, no origin, a non-GitHub origin, and a host error. Admission and `athena check` pass with no personal-data allow-list changes.
